title: Sectionwise and multiplicative normalization of closed-source site exchange
statement:
Fix the finite datum $A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions] and a $k$-scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme]. For closed immersions $C,D\hookrightarrow X$, put $I=C\times_XD$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product]. Write $P_C^e=i_*A_C$ and $P_C^p=i_*A_C$ for the etale and pro-etale constant module direct images, and $\mu^e_{C,D}$ and $\mu^p_{C,D}$ for restriction of both sections to $I$, followed by multiplication. Use precisely the etale sources and multiplications of [lem-pur-etale-closed-constant-tensor] and the pro-etale ones of [def-pur-supported-cup]. Let $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proet}}\to X_{\mathrm{et}}$ be site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $q_C:\nu_X^*P_C^e\cong P_C^p$ and, for a scheme map $v:X'\to X$, $b^p_{v,C}:v_p^*P_C^p\cong P_{C'}^p$ ($C'=X'\times_XC$) be the already specified canonical exchanges of [lem-pur-supported-constant-exchange-normalization].

The section map of this particular $q_C$, for every weakly etale $y:Y\to X$, is the composite
$$(\nu_X^*P_C^e)(Y)\cong\Gamma(Y_{\mathrm{et}},y_e^*P_C^e)\cong\Gamma((Y\times_XC)_{\mathrm{et}},A)\cong\Gamma((Y\times_XC)_{\mathrm{proet}},A)=P_C^p(Y).$$
Here the first identification is the comparison-section formula of [lem-cbc-comparison-pullback-sections], the second uses the specified etale closed exchange, and the third is degree-zero canonical comparison [lem-cbc-abelian-etale-proetale-cohomology-comparison]. These maps preserve restriction in $Y$ and the $A$-action.

With the canonical tensor comparisons understood, these specified maps satisfy
$$q_I\nu_X^*(\mu^e_{C,D})=\mu^p_{C,D}(q_C\otimes q_D),$$
$$b^p_{v,I}v_p^*(\mu^p_{C,D})=\mu^p_{C',D'}(b^p_{v,C}\otimes b^p_{v,D}).$$
Both equalities hold for sheaf tensors and in the ordinary derived category with the degree-zero flat models of the cited source constructions and the derived pullback tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The maps here are the actual restriction-and-multiplication maps on arbitrary weakly etale tests, including empty or nonreduced supports, and $v$ is arbitrary.

proof.text: Identify the prescribed gamma with the standard mate of the lower-star comparison, followed by the constant-unit identification. Both maps have the same monoidal unit normalization; uniqueness in the supported constant exchange theorem identifies them. The comparison adjunction unit commutes with this mate. At the terminal object, lower-star comparison is identity and naturality along the canonical terminal pullback isomorphism gives the constant section comparison.

proof.text: For a weakly etale test Y, identify the prescribed pro-etale exchange with the standard weakly etale base-change mate followed by constant inverse image. The defining closed adjunction transpose, the mate-counit identity, and the existing weakly etale base-change mate formula give this identification. The localization restriction base-change formula, naturality of constant inverse image, and the universal property of the two pullbacks identify its terminal evaluation with proSupportSections. The comparison square for normalized exchanges and naturality of the comparison adjunction unit then give the required section formula. Invertibility follows from the stated etale closed exchange and comparison adjunction unit. Restriction compatibility is naturality of gamma and scalar compatibility is linearity of its module components.

proof.text: The cokernel presentations of supported constants make each constant restriction epic. Right exactness of tensor makes their tensor epic; both inverse-image functors preserve epimorphisms. Precompose each desired multiplication square with this tensor of restrictions. The defining normalization of etale and pro-etale multiplication, oplax monoidal naturality, and the monoidal unit identity reduce both sides to restriction to the intersection. For scheme pullback the canonical support-change map preserves restriction by adjunction unit normalization and lower-star composition. Cancel the epic tensor to conclude.

proof.text: Prove a general degree-zero derived-square lemma for an exact additive strong monoidal left adjoint preserving flat objects. The canonical single-complex tensor isomorphism is natural and commutes with the cochain oplax tensor comparison: check degree zero using the two single-object evaluation isomorphisms and the bifunctor coproduct inclusion, and use zero objects in other degrees. Thus each ordinary multiplication square gives a cochain square. The counit identifying the left-derived functor with its exact cochain functor is natural and satisfies the existing leftDerivedTensorComparison identity. Transport the cochain square through this identity and the canonical single/left-derived isomorphism. Apply it to the two already proved ordinary squares.
